The two central characters, Ilse and Jonas, are written as complex characters with a rich, shared backstory and nuanced emotional depth. Through subtle observations—such as Ilse remembering Jonas's childhood refusal to wear a hood in the rain, his defensive tone at the kitchen table with Henning, and her quiet restraint in not pointing out his broken shoe sole—their strained yet caring mother-son dynamic feels deeply human and believable. 

Meanwhile, the minor character—the delivery van driver on the opposite bank—is developed at an appropriate level of complexity for his brief role. Although he serves a functional purpose in the scene (creating a sense of time pressure and giving Ilse a reason to cross the river), the detail that he crosses at the exact same time every Thursday yet still feels the need to flash his headlights impatiently gives him a distinct human quirk. This ensures he feels like a organic part of Ilse's everyday world rather than a mere plot device.
